newsitem.title: USA: Price bought much of Cramer's Dow stake - sources.
newsitem.headline: Price bought much of Cramer's Dow stake - sources.

text.p: Money manager Michael Price scooped up a big chunk of Dow Jones & Co Inc stock recently sold by hedge fund manager James Cramer, according to market sources.
Price bought about 500,000 shares at $38 per share, according to the sources. Dow Jones shares were up 1/4 to 39-7/8 early Thursday afternoon.
Cramer, president of Cramer Berkowitz & Co, sold most of the one million shares of Dow Jones that he controlled, his office said Thursday.
Fortune magazine reported that Cramer sold the shares over two days in late May.
Price declined comment on whether he bought Cramer's stake. Cramer also declined comment.
In an interview with Reuters, Price did confirm that he had recently increased his stake in Dow and said he would be "patient" in holding his position.
He said he continued to expect the company to either sell or spin off its electronic information unit, Dow Jones Markets, formerly known as Telerate.
"I think they ought to spin out or sell Telerate," he said.
"I'm still of that opinion and believe it's going to happen," he said. "We are very patient, and have a lot of staying power. We're not going away."
As of April, Price's Mutual Series mutual funds owned about 4.1 million of Dow Jones's 95 million outstanding shares.
Cramer had tried to pressure Dow Jones to sell Dow Jones Markets. According to Fortune, he grew impatient at not being able to get management to sell.
Dow Jones announced in January that it planned to invest as much as $650 million over the next three years to strengthen the unit.
"We think that in American business, the right thing happens sooner or later," Price said. "When it happens sooner, you have a greater rate of return."
Price said he feels the Dow Jones board is "very smart...and (chairman) Peter Kann is a very good listener."
"The right decisions are going to get made," Price said. "That's why we own the stock. We think the (stock) value will go higher."
